rows.title: 9-2X 2.5L EJ253 Head Gasket External Leak (Subaru-Sourced)
rows.howToFix: Head gasket replacement (~$1,800-$2,800 at Subaru-experienced independent). Use Subaru OEM MLS gaskets (Mahle aftermarket also acceptable). ALWAYS resurface the heads — warped surfaces are common cause of recurrent leak. Timing belt, water pump, all idlers should be replaced at the same time since engine is apart.

rows.title: 9-3 Direct Ignition Cassette (DIC) Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace DIC ($150-$350 OEM cassette, $80-$180 aftermarket — quality matters here, cheap units fail in months). DIY ~30 minutes with a 10mm hex socket. Always replace spark plugs at the same time (NGK PFR7S8EG or equivalent). Carry a spare DIC if traveling long distances — failure is sudden but the car limps home on the remaining cylinders.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: 9-3 Second-Gen Front Lower Control Arm Bushing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace lower control arms as a pair (Lemförder OEM ~$120-$200 each, plus $200-$400 labor). DIY-friendly with a spring compressor and basic tools. Polyurethane aftermarket bushings (Powerflex) are more durable but transmit more NVH. Get a 4-wheel alignment after the job.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: 9-3 Sentronic (Aisin AF33-5) 5-Speed Auto Failure
rows.howToFix: Drain-and-fill ATF every 40,000-50,000 miles with Aisin AFW+ / JWS3309 (~$120-$200 DIY — ~6 quarts come out per service). If shifts are already harsh, valve body rebuild ($800-$1,500) or full transmission swap with used unit ($1,500-$2,800). New AF33 transmissions are hard to source for Saab post-bankruptcy — used is the practical option.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: 9-3 Sunroof Drain Clog → Soaked Carpet → DICE/TWICE Module Failure
rows.howToFix: Clear sunroof drains annually (compressed air from above, fishline gently from below). If carpet is wet, dry IMMEDIATELY — remove driver carpet and inspect the modules. Once a module is corroded the only fix is replacement and recoding ($300-$1,200). Aftermarket dehumidifier packs in footwell help in humid climates.

rows.title: 9-3 B207 Turbo Bearing Failure
rows.howToFix: Replacement turbo ($400-$800 reman, $800-$1,400 OEM new) plus oil-feed line ($50-$80) and gaskets. Total job ~$1,200-$2,000 at independent. Always replace the oil-feed line — old line is the most common reason a fresh turbo fails immediately. Bypass valve ($40-$80) at the same time.

rows.title: 9-5 B235 Turbo Oil Sludge — Class Action Settlement
rows.howToFix: Strict 3,000-5,000 mile oil intervals with full-synthetic 5W-30 (or 5W-40 for high-mileage) — Mobil 1 or Amsoil. Sludge-removal cycle (BG EPR, Liqui Moly Pro-Line) over multiple oil changes. Inspect the oil pickup screen if sump removed — heavy sludge means engine rebuild ($3,000-$5,000). Original class-action coverage long-expired.

rows.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor (CPS) Hot No-Start
rows.howToFix: Replace the crankshaft position sensor with an OEM/Bosch-quality part - cheap unbranded aftermarket sensors are reported to fail again within months. The sensor is relatively inexpensive but located awkwardly near the bell-housing.

rows.title: 9-5 Direct Ignition Cassette (DIC) Failure
rows.howToFix: Replacement DIC ($150-$350 OEM, $80-$180 aftermarket). NGK PFR7S8EG plugs at the same time. Trionic 7 ECU on 1999+ models compensates for misfire well, so the car often limps home — but P03xx codes will accumulate. Some owners pre-emptively replace at 100,000 miles.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Direct Ignition Cassette (DIC) Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the Direct Ignition Cassette (use a quality OEM-grade unit) and renew the spark plugs at the same time, applying the correct Saab dielectric plug. Fixing any valve-cover gasket leak prevents repeat failures.

rows.title: Engine Oil Sludge in 2.0T/2.3T Four-Cylinder
rows.howToFix: Install the updated PCV #6 breather kit, switch to full synthetic oil with short 3,000-5,000 mile change intervals, and if sludge is suspected drop the sump and clean it (including the oil-pickup screen) thoroughly. Severe cases require engine rebuild or replacement.

rows.title: SID Display Dead/Missing Pixels
rows.howToFix: Replace the LCD ribbon cable (cheap DIY kits exist, no soldering needed) or fit a replacement LCD module. Professional pixel-repair services are also available. The unit itself usually does not need full replacement.

rows.title: 9-5 Saab Information Display (SID) Missing-Pixel Failure
rows.howToFix: Rebuild option: send the SID to a specialist (BBA Reman, Module Master, or several European Saab specialists) for ribbon-cable resoldering — $80-$180 with return shipping. DIY repair kits with replacement flex-cable available for ~$30. Replacement used SID rarely fixes the issue — they age the same way.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Fuel Line Leak from Damaged Pump Retaining Tabs - NHTSA Recall 07V087
rows.howToFix: If fuel is smelled or seen, switch off the engine, avoid sparks or flames, move people away and arrange safe towing or emergency assistance. Check the VIN at NHTSA or with an authorized service provider. For an open campaign 07V087, the recall remedy is installation of the specified retaining bracket at no charge; do not improvise a clamp or disturb a leaking connection. Do not buy a fuel pump, line, seal or bracket from this page; recall completion and the exact remedy must be confirmed by VIN.

rows.title: V6 Ignition Discharge Module (IGBT) Overheating - NHTSA Recall 05V399/06V410
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN for open campaigns 05V399 and 06V410 and have the authorized recall inspection or module replacement completed if applicable. For a stall, no-start or ignition DTC on a vehicle with completed campaigns, diagnose module power, wiring, engine management and other causes using WIS before replacing parts. Do not buy an ignition discharge module from this page; VIN campaign status, B308 application, bank, installed module and diagnosis determine the remedy.

rows.title: 5-Speed Automatic Transmission Limp Mode / Valve Body Faults
rows.howToFix: Diagnose for solenoid/speed-sensor codes; a revised valve body (2003+ units are far more durable) or solenoid replacement often resolves it. Critically, change to synthetic ATF every 50,000-60,000 miles to prevent recurrence.

rows.title: 9-7X Driver-Door Master Power Window Switch Fire Recall (NHTSA 12V-406 + 14V-404)
rows.howToFix: Check VIN at NHTSA recall lookup (12V-406 / 14V-404). Free dealer remedy: inspect part number on the door module and install a new switch module if affected. GM advised parking outside until the remedy is performed. If you smell burning plastic from the driver door, do not operate the window — get the recall fix scheduled immediately.

rows.title: Classic 900 (1979-1993) Windshield Frame & Rear Wheel Arch Rust
rows.howToFix: Annual inspection at the windshield frame (lift the trim moldings) and rear wheel arches. Treatment of pinhole rust early ($200-$500) is far cheaper than structural repair ($1,500-$5,000) once advanced. Convertibles have additional rust at the chassis stiffening members. SaabClub specialists in the US Northeast offer body restoration packages.
